# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

I should wait and let the others send me information first — Deaf can see the bomb, Mute reads the manual. Since I come second in the order (Mute, Blind, Deaf), Mute has already spoken this round but I received nothing, meaning either Mute sent nothing or it didn't reach me. I'll wait.

Deaf says: Bomb report. Display reads zero. Light is orange. Three wires: wire one red, wire two yellow, wire three blue. That is everything I can see. Mute, I received your four symbols but I do not yet know what they mean. Blind, this is the bomb as it appears to me.

The rejection was because "👂" is not in the gesture alphabet. The allowed symbols are: 👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳.

So I'll replace the illegal symbol. My intent: speak to Mute asking for the manual rule, and gesture to Deaf to nudge them to decode and relay Mute's symbols. I'll use only legal symbols.

```
speak(to="mute", text="This is Blind. I am the hands. I can reach the bomb but I cannot see it, and I cannot see your gestures. Deaf tells me: display reads zero, light is orange, wires are red one, yellow two, blue three. I need the manual's rule for this exact configuration. Please gesture the rule to Deaf as clearly as you can, one symbol per concept.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🙏", "✊", "👆"])
```

Deaf says: Update. Display still reads zero. Light has changed from orange to green. Wires unchanged: one red, two yellow, three blue. Mute, I have your three symbols and Blind's three symbols, but I still have no code to read them. Tell me plainly what the symbols mean — I will relay to Blind. Blind, do not touch anything yet; I have no instruction for you.

I'm the Blind monkey. New info: light changed orange → green, display still zero, wires unchanged (1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue). Deaf got my 3 gestures but can't decode them without a key; Deaf also got Mute's symbols and can't decode those either. The core problem: nobody has established a shared meaning for gestures. Mute reads the manual but can't speak; Mute can gesture, but Deaf can't interpret gestures without a code, and I can't see gestures at all. Channels: I (Blind) speak → Mute receives. I gesture → Deaf and Mute receive. Deaf speaks → I receive (and Mute? Deaf can't hear; Deaf's speech reaches whoever can hear = Mute and Blind). Actually Deaf speaks, and those who can hear receive: Mute and Blind. Mute speaks? Mute cannot speak. So Mute's only output is gestures, which reach Deaf and Blind—but Blind can't see gestures (I receive one blank per symbol, knowing something was signalled but not what).

So the bottleneck: Mute's manual knowledge can only leave Mute via gesture. Deaf sees gestures but has no code. I can't see gestures. The only way to transmit the manual rule is: Mute gestures → Deaf sees → Deaf must decode → Deaf speaks it to me. But Deaf can't decode without a key.

Key insight: I can establish a code. I speak to Mute (Mute hears me). I can propose a mapping: e.g., "gesture one symbol to mean the cut position." But Deaf needs to interpret too. Since Deaf already sees Mute's symbols, I can define meaning by counting/ordering. Better: ask Mute to gesture the answer in a self-describing way — but Deaf still needs the key.

Simplest robust approach: I define a code in words to Mute, and simultaneously tell Deaf the same code (Deaf hears my speech? No—Deaf cannot hear. Deaf only sees my gestures). Hmm. So I can't tell Deaf a code in words. I can only gesture to Deaf.

So: I gesture a code to Deaf (Deaf sees symbols), and I speak the same code to Mute (Mute hears words). Both get the same mapping. Then Mute gestures the manual's answer using that code, Deaf decodes and speaks it to me.

But that's heavy. Alternative: the manual likely maps (display, light, wire colors) → which wire to cut. I need the rule. Let me just ask Mute directly via speech for the rule in words, and ask Mute to gesture it to Deaf, and ask Deaf to relay. But Deaf can't decode arbitrary gestures.

Let me set a minimal code now. I'll speak to Mute: "Use this code: gesture ✊=wire1, ✌=wire2, ✌✌... " too complex. Simpler: Mute gestures a single number of symbols? Mute can gesture a count. Let me have Mute signal the cut position by gesturing that many identical symbols, e.g., ✊ repeated N times = cut wire N. Deaf can count. I'll tell Deaf: "count the symbols Mute sends; the count is the wire to cut." And tell Mute the same.

Actually even simpler and more reliable: I'll speak to Mute asking for the rule, and tell Mute: "gesture to Deaf using: ✊=1, ✌=2, ✌ repeated... " no.

Let me just define: number of symbols = wire number. Tell both. Then Mute gestures N symbols, Deaf counts N, speaks "cut wire N" to me, I cut.

Let me do that. Also acknowledge Deaf's update.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here. New state: display zero, light green, wires red-yellow-blue. I need the manual's rule for this exact state. To send me the answer, use this code: gesture to Deaf a number of identical symbols equal to the wire to cut. One symbol means cut wire 1, two symbols means cut wire 2, three means wire 3. Deaf will count them and tell me. Please send that now.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👆", "👆", "👆"])
```

What I should send: to Deaf, gesture something to indicate "I feel nothing / no reading yet" — but gestures are limited to symbols and Deaf can't decode arbitrary ones. Better: speak to Mute (who hears me) to coordinate, and gesture to Deaf minimally.

Actually the crucial channel: I can speak to Mute. Mute can gesture to Deaf. Deaf speaks to me. So I should use my speech to Mute to drive the confirmation, and use my gesture to Deaf to acknowledge.

Hmm, but Deaf might interpret my 👍 as answering something. Let me be careful and instead gesture to Deaf a sequence that I can define in speech to Mute... no, Deaf can't hear.

Simplest: gesture 👍 to Deaf (agreement/yes to the count hypothesis), and speak to Mute to nail the exact mapping.

speak(to="mute", text="Blind here. I feel nothing on the bomb yet — my hands have no reading until I act, so I have no independent info. Deaf sees your symbol counts: orange=4, green=3, red=2.
